淑.meaning: Your <part>uncle</part> takes up ballet at sixty. At the recital he leaps through a mist of <part>water drops</part> from the fog machine, lands without a sound on the tip of one toe, and bows. The whole hall gasps: he's <kanji>graceful</kanji>.
淑.on: Afterwards he sips his tea, little finger raised, and drops in one <sound>su</sound>gar <sound>cu</sound>be.
淑.kun: His dance partner joins him for the encore: <sound>she</sound> spins him round like a <sound>to</sound>p, and neither of them wobbles.

篤.meaning: A <part>horse</part> learns that the panda next door eats only <part>bamboo</part>. Every dawn, through storms and snow, she gallops to the far grove and back with one fresh shoot in her teeth. She never misses a day: her devotion is <kanji>fervent</kanji>.
篤.on: The panda sets its clock by her hooves: tick-<sound>tock</sound>, clip-clop.
篤.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>... <sound>tsu</sound>!' sneezes the panda, as the snowy horse shakes herself off at the door.

堪.meaning: A tiny seed under the <part>soil</part> gets <part>tremendously</part> squashed: a cow lies on it, a tractor parks on it, a circus elephant naps on it. Every spring it still pokes up one green leaf. That seed can <kanji>withstand</kanji> anything.
堪.on: Its roots dig a long <sound>tun</sound>nel under the whole farm.
堪.kun: A mole pops out of the tunnel and leaves the brave leaf a <sound>ta</sound>co as a prize.

熊.meaning: At a talent show, a huge furry contestant shows off every <part>ability</part>: juggling, tap dancing, then strolling barefoot across <part>hot coals</part> without a flinch. The judges wonder who's inside the costume, until he roars. It's a real <kanji>bear</kanji>.
熊.on: He wins first prize: a ride round the stage on a <sound>u</sound>nicorn.
熊.kun: He shares his prize <sound>coo</sound>kie with his <sound>ma</sound>ma in the front row.

該.meaning: In court, the judge gives a long <part>speech</part>: 'the said hoop', 'the said ladder', 'the said acrobat'. Each time, the <part>acrobat</part> in the dock flips and points at the very thing he means, so nobody forgets which one: the <kanji>above-stated</kanji> one.
該.on: A <sound>gui</sound>de dog in the public gallery nods along every time.

峠.meaning: A snail sets off over a <part>mountain</part>. For a week the path points <part>above</part>, inch after inch, then at the very top it tips <part>below</part>, and he slides the rest of the way on his shell, cheering. Where up turns into down is the <kanji>mountain pass</kanji>.
峠.kun: At the top, a hiker resting there stubs her <sound>toe</sound> on a sleeping <sound>ge</sound>cko.

娯.meaning: Every Friday the <part>woman</part> who runs the post office decides to <part>give</part> herself the afternoon off: kites, a jigsaw, a nap in a hammock. The sign on her door just says 'Gone for <kanji>recreation</kanji>'.
娯.on: This Friday it's snorkelling, so she packs her <sound>go</sound>ggles.
